text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Nearly 1,200 Italian, French and Spanish troops will land from in Albania today at the start of the Italian-led security mission to the Balkan country (all).

* Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) leader Massimo D'Alema harshly criticised foreign minister Lamberto Dini's ouverture towards centre-right opposition saying there was no alternative to the current centre-left government coalition (all).

* Hard left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said Italy's welfare state needs reforms that could lead to increased spending in some areas but pensions should be the last subject discussed in talks. Bertinotti said cuts in pension spending ought to be avoided for 10 years (all).

* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed Italy's gross domestic product (GDP) rose by 0.1 pecent year-on-year in the fourth quarter of 1996. Istat also confirmed GDP grew 0.7 percent in 1996 against 2.9 percent in 1995. Growth of GDP in Italy is the slowest among G7 nations(all).

* Prime minister Romano Prodi said the Italian government was studying whether to tranfer the 35 percent stake in SGS-Thomson Microelectronics NV held by state holding IRI to IRI's engineering unit Finmeccanica (all).

* Shares in information technology group Olivetti fell 5.9 percent on the Milan bourse ahead of a board meeting today to examine 1996 results, seen confirming January's statement of pre-tax losses of around 800 billion lire (Sole 24 Ore).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
